claims.text: The initial feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Current HVAF-i7 processing of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces acceptable coating quality.
Current HVAF-i7 processing of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces insufficient coating thickness.
Increasing particle velocity in the HVAF-i7 process will increase deposition efficiency.
Increased deposition efficiency will enable thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coats.
The velocity-modified HVAF-i7 process will produce adequately adherent FeCoNiCrAl bond coats comparable to coatings achieved using HVAF-M3.
Adjusting process-gas flow rate and nozzle configuration can increase particle velocity during HVAF-i7 spraying.
Increasing particle velocity increases in-flight particle kinetic energy.
Greater in-flight kinetic energy improves particle impact and splat formation on the substrate.
Higher impact energy promotes greater particle deformation upon impact.
Greater particle deformation promotes better bonding to the substrate or preceding splats.
Improved impact bonding increases deposition efficiency.
The modified process will produce denser coatings.
The modified process will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The modified HVAF-i7 process will yield a statistically significant thickness increase relative to the standard HVAF-i7 baseline.
The modified HVAF-i7 process will maintain adhesion comparable to the standard HVAF-i7 baseline.
The intervention will remain effective for deposition inside substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention will remain effective provided that increased velocity does not cause excessive in-flight oxidation or microstructural damage.
